findings.headline: Peak stress at lap 21 did not affect pace – monitor early wet‑dry transition stress
findings.detail: Stress spiked to 100 at lap 21 while the driver was on intermediate tyre age 2, lapping backmarkers under blue flags on a wet track (22.1 °C). Pace delta was 0 s, indicating the driver maintained median pace despite the stress, so the high stress did not translate into a time loss. The engineer should monitor stress triggers around early wet‑to‑dry transitions but no immediate pace‑related action is required.

findings.headline: Medium tyres gained pace as track dried; brief loss on lap 40 suggests earlier soft switch
findings.detail: When the medium tyres came on lap 38 the modelled degradation turned negative (‑0.383 s/lap) and pace delta fell to –0.497 s on lap 39, showing the medium brought a performance gain as the track dried (track temp 24.2 °C). However, a +0.497 s delta on lap 40 coincided with the first dry‑track crossover and a blue flag, suggesting the driver lost the medium’s advantage briefly. The engineer should consider a slightly earlier medium‑to‑soft switch to lock in the gain before the dry crossover.

findings.headline: Soft tyres delivered peak speed but suffered large delta when blue‑flagged; avoid traffic early in soft stint
findings.detail: The soft tyre stint (laps 48‑50) produced the fastest lap of the race (89.707 s) but also a +7.010 s delta on lap 49, likely caused by a blue‑flag encounter on a dry track (25.2 °C). Stress reading of 85.6 on lap 50 is post‑race, so cannot confirm fatigue impact. The engineer should note that softs are highly sensitive to traffic; a clean lap early in the stint could extract more consistent gain.
